For 46 years, the Raul Jimenez Thanksgiving Dinner has brought San Antonio together for one of the largest holiday gatherings in the country. On a day centered on thanks and gratitude, we are honored to be part of this tradition once again. 🦃

To help keep it going, more than two dozen of our team members and their loved ones spent the eve before the big meal preparing the feast that serves nearly 30,000 neighbors in need each year. That includes more than 500 turkeys and 18,000 pounds of stuffing, yams and green beans shared at one big community dinner table. 🍽️

Founded in 1979 by San Antonio restaurateur Raul Jimenez, the event was created to help ensure seniors and those less fortunate could celebrate Thanksgiving with dignity and fellowship. All these years later, it continues to offer much more than a hot meal. Guests enjoy live music, entertainment and the warmth that comes from a community that shows up for one another year after year. 🏘️

That’s why we’re proud to stand alongside the organizers, volunteers and sponsors who make this tradition possible. 🧡

#HappyThanksgiving #RaulJimenez #SanAntonio #MarathonPetroleum #MPCGives 🫶

For #FlashbackFriday, we brought an old black-and-white photo to life with color. Back then, the "Best in the Long Run" slogan became a familiar sight for drivers, just like Marathon ⛽ stations continue to be across the country today!

ICYMI: Two MPC terminals were recently recognized by the EPA’s ENERGY STAR® Challenge for Industry for reducing energy intensity by 10% or more within five years.

At our Anchorage T2, Alaska, terminal, energy use dropped 29.4% in just two years, while our Mount Vernon, Indiana, terminal saw a 20.7% reduction over four years.

MPC’s Vice President of Terminals, Regina Zolnor, said, “We are proud of our energy management strategy and contributing to the work recognized by the EPA’s ENERGY STAR program.”

The ENERGY STAR Challenge for Industry encourages manufacturers across the country to reduce energy use and operate more efficiently.
